case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: The knowledge test encompassed the topics IoT. Each test question had 10 multiple-choice questions worth a total of 10 points.
object_definition: Codified facts and procedures about IoT component identification, placement, and connectivity.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: The paper group utilized a book manual as an assistance tool. The paper-based guidelines contained written assembly instructions and images of the IoT components.
object_definition: Written text and static diagrams describing assembly steps.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: The MAR application visualizes IoT circuit assembly steps, provides 3D models of circuit components, and enables user interaction.
object_definition: Step-by-step 3D animated models and textual guidance overlaid on breadboard.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: The MAR group (0.5 error rate) made fewer errors than the paper group (1.35 error rate). The MAR group showed a significant reduction in errors (Z=-3.480, p=0.001).
object_definition: Hands-on ability to place components correctly without mistakes.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: AR aids in information integration by associating virtual objects with real-world objects. The 3D model animation guides the user to follow the assembly positioning.
object_definition: Ability to mentally map component placement onto physical breadboard holes.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: Both groups were able to retain the knowledge which is from immediate post-test to delayed post-test. No statistically significant change (MAR p=0.886, paper p=0.914).
object_definition: Memory of the correct sequence of assembly actions after one week.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: 40 participants, including 22 females 18 males, consisting of Degree students (36), Master (2), and PhD (2).
object_definition: University students who took part in the experiment.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: 20 participants in the MAR group (10 male, 10 female).
object_definition: Subset of participants who used the MAR application.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: 20 participants in the paper group (8 male, 12 female).
object_definition: Subset of participants who used the paper manual.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: Participants were required to read the paper manual as part of the traditional learning intervention. While assembling, they repeatedly referred to the paper manual.
object_definition: Learning intervention using a physical book manual with text and images.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: The MAR application learning intervention was conducted. AR displayed assembly steps to aid participants in constructing the Arduino-based IoT circuit.
object_definition: Learning intervention using mobile augmented reality with 3D animated overlays.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: An iPad Pro was chosen for its high computational power and large screen, ensuring stable AR-tracking and a better user experience.
object_definition: Hardware device running the MAR application.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: A marker-based AR application was developed using the Vuforia Engine to track image targets.
object_definition: Software engine for marker-based tracking.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: The development involved creating 3D models and animations for various IoT components. The step-by-step animation of virtual elements navigated the accurate placement.
object_definition: Digital assets showing virtual components and their movement.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: A QR code served as the AR marker, placed on the breadboard to ensure accurate 3D model rendering during assembly.
object_definition: Physical QR code used for tracking.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: The MAR application ... user interface in AR was developed to control the IoT components.
object_definition: The custom-built mobile app for AR guidance.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: Extraneous elements often cause cognitive overload, particularly for inexperienced learners who may struggle to focus on relevant parts. Paper group required calculating connection slots from diagram ... significant cognitive effort.
object_definition: Mental overburden due to irrelevant or poorly visualized information.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: Paper group participants commented ... no clear position indicator on the physical IoT circuit component, unlike the MAR method. Identifying appropriate hole positions ... requires significant cognitive effort.
object_definition: Inability to perceive 3D placement from 2D static diagrams.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: The paper approach required participants to switch their attention between the task at hand and reading instructions.
object_definition: Time and mental cost of alternating between reading and doing.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: Participants also complain about the jittery visualization that affects the 3D model alignment with the breadboard, which impacts their judgment about the component assemble position.
object_definition: Unstable AR overlay causing misalignment.

case_title: Evaluating Knowledge Gain and Retention in IoT Circuit Assembly Using Mobile Augmented Reality Technology
evidence_statement: Participants also mentioned that 'we were unable to realize our mistakes during the assembly task, which led us to be unsuccessful in building the circuit in which the LED lamp was not lit up.'
object_definition: No real-time feedback or error checking in the MAR system.
